mike: Heads up — noticed a sharp p95 increase for qwen2.5 serving after the kernel-selector change (commit 2c4a9f). p50 stable ~45ms, p95 jumped from ~80ms to ~230ms across the canary pool :thinking_face:

raj: Saw this too. Quick profiler dump points at repeated KV cache invalidations + a memcpy hotspot when sequence length crosses tokenizer boundary (~512->520). Kernel selector is flipping to the 'fused_attn_fast' path for seq>512 which assumes aligned kv_head dims.

sophia: paste of profiler snippet:
```
[profiler] qwen2.5-7b 2026-03-18 10:02:01
hotspots:
  memcpy: 38.2% (kv cache flushes)
  attn_fused_kernel: 27.5%
  scalar_attn_fallback: 2.1%
warnings:
  kv_head_mismatch detected for request id 0x9b7f (attn_heads=32, kv_heads=16, head_dim=64)
```

mike: That kv_head_mismatch warning is interesting — we usually keep kv_heads == attn_heads but qwen2.5 variants sometimes use head packing for kv which the fast kernel didn't anticipate. Also seen odd token splits when input mixes CJK + roman script; tokenizer returns extra prefix tokens and the runtime re-shards KV which triggers the eviction logic.

ben: Repro steps I used locally (loadgen):
```bash
./loadgen --model qwen2.5-7b --seq 520 --batch 8 --inputs multilingual-cjk-samples.txt --ramp 60s
# p95 reproduces within 30s
```
Swapping kernel back to legacy `attn_slow_vectorized` fixes p95 down to ~95ms in my env.

perf-bot: [alert] Canary pool: qwen2.5 p95 regression > 2x since 2026-03-18T09:40Z. Link: https://console.redwood/pools/canary/alerts/8921 :rotating_light:

raj: I started a bisect across kernel-selector commits. Early results: commit range 2c4a9f..2c76d10 introduces the aggressive fused path rule (seq>512 => fused). Reverting that rule removes the regression. We should either: tighten kernel predicate (require kv_head == attn_head) OR make fused kernel tolerant to kv-head packing.

sophia: Quick runtime guard proposal: when selecting fused_attn_fast, check: `if (attn_head_count != kv_head_count || head_dim % 64 != 0) skip_fused()`. Also add unit test for tokenizer fence-case where token count jumps across boundary (seq 508->520) with mixed-script input.

mike: Agreed. Short-term: patch runtime to add the predicate guard and push canary. Medium-term: update fused kernel to handle kv-head packing and add a kernel-level assertion to avoid silent mem copies.

ben: Draft patch snippet I tested (works locally):
```diff
@@ runtime/kernel_selector.cc
- if (seq_len > 512) return KERNEL_FUSED_FAST;
+ if (seq_len > 512 && attn_heads == kv_heads && (head_dim & 63) == 0) return KERNEL_FUSED_FAST;
+ // fallback to legacy vectorized path otherwise
```
Can push as hotfix canary once CI passes.

raj: After applying that guard in my canary run, p95 dropped from 228ms -> 102ms and stability improved. I'll open the PR and include perf comparison table.

sophia: I'll add the tokenizer fuzz testcase and a small KV-head parity check in the model descriptor loader so we log model variants that intentionally pack kv heads. That'll help avoid surprises.

mike: Action items: raj PR for hotfix (owner: raj), sophia add tests + model metadata check (owner: sophia), ben prepare rollback patch in case hotfix causes any unexpected slowdowns (owner: ben). Schedule a short canary watch 30m after deploy and mark esk status if p95 > 150ms. Thanks all :thumbsup:
